skill.name: minimal-run-and-audit
skill.description: Runs a selected short reproduction command, captures execution evidence, extracts metrics, tracks repository changes, and prepares standardized reproduction reports.
skill.summary: Run and audit short machine learning reproduction commands with normalized evidence.
skill.author: lllllllama

security_audit.summary: The runner intentionally executes a user-supplied command, which is a confirmed high-risk capability despite avoiding shell interpretation. Two parent-directory references cross the audited package boundary, and the output wrapper dynamically executes a Python module; Markdown backticks and reporting text are false positives.

remediation.issue: The runner executes any command supplied through the command argument.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation and run commands in a constrained environment with documented executable and path controls.

remediation.issue: Skill instructions reference files outside the audited skill directory.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the required guidance inside the skill and use package-local paths so all instructions are included in the audit.

remediation.issue: The output wrapper imports and executes an ancestor module without integrity verification.
remediation.suggestion: Vendor the writer into the package or verify a pinned module digest before loading it.

content.value_statement: Short reproduction runs often produce inconsistent evidence and unclear results. This skill executes a selected command and organizes outcomes, metrics, logs, and repository changes.
actual_capabilities: Executes a selected non-training command with a configurable timeout.
Captures standard output, standard error, exit status, and timeout state.
Extracts numeric metrics from command output using a defined text pattern.
Compares Git status before and after execution to identify changed paths.
Classifies runs as successful, partial, or blocked and prepares normalized evidence.
limitations: It does not select the reproduction target or design the experiment.
It does not install dependencies, obtain assets, or configure environments.
It is intended for short verification commands, not training or long-running jobs.
Automatic metric extraction may misidentify values in unstructured output.

use_cases.title: Verify a documented inference command
use_cases.description: Run a repository inference example and capture its outcome, logs, metrics, and file changes.

use_cases.title: Audit a reproduction smoke test
use_cases.description: Produce concise evidence showing whether a selected smoke test succeeded, failed, or timed out.

use_cases.title: Normalize evaluation evidence
use_cases.description: Convert a short evaluation attempt into consistent artifacts for team review and comparison.

prompt_templates.title: Run a smoke test
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the selected smoke command in [repository path] with a [timeout] second limit. Report the outcome and captured evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner has one documented command and needs a clear result.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an inference example
prompt_templates.prompt: Execute [inference command] in [repository path]. Capture logs, numeric metrics, timeout state, and repository changes without modifying scientific behavior.
prompt_templates.scenario: An engineer needs evidence from a documented inference workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Compare an evaluation result
prompt_templates.prompt: Run [evaluation command] and compare the observed metric with [expected baseline]. Mark unsupported comparisons and document any changed files.
prompt_templates.scenario: A reviewer needs a bounded comparison against a published or documented baseline.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a patched reproduction
prompt_templates.prompt: Execute [command] after the approved patches. Separate execution facts from inferences and document patch effects, comparability limits, metrics, and blockers.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced reproduction includes controlled repository changes requiring traceable evidence.

output_examples.input: Run the documented CPU smoke test with a 60 second timeout.
output_examples.output: Status: successful. The command completed within the limit, produced one accuracy metric, and created no repository changes.

output_examples.input: Run the evaluation command and record why it stops.
output_examples.output: Status: blocked. The executable was unavailable, so no evaluation metric was observed and no files changed.

output_examples.input: Audit a command that exceeds the allowed runtime.
output_examples.output: Status: partial. The command timed out after the configured limit, and the available output was retained for review.

best_practices: Confirm the exact command, repository path, and timeout before execution.
Use short documented inference, evaluation, smoke, or sanity commands.
Review reported file changes and disclose any effect on scientific meaning.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill to start training or resume long-running jobs.
Do not treat extracted metrics as validated scientific conclusions.
Do not hide preprocessing, checkpoint, evaluation, or metric changes.

faq.question: What commands can this skill run?
faq.answer: It can run a selected executable with arguments. Use it only for short, trusted, non-training verification commands.

faq.question: Does it use a shell?
faq.answer: The runner tokenizes the command and launches the executable directly. Shell operators and expansions are not interpreted.

faq.question: How are metrics collected?
faq.answer: It scans command output for named numeric values and selects a likely primary metric.

faq.question: How are file changes detected?
faq.answer: It compares Git status snapshots taken before and after the command.

faq.question: Can it run model training?
faq.answer: No. The skill explicitly excludes training startup, resume operations, and long-running training state.

faq.question: Does it prove reproduction success?
faq.answer: No. It records execution evidence and comparability limits, but scientific validation still requires expert review.
